subject: SlateBridge dedicated sizing — throughput, SLO fit, buffer proposal
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@slatebridge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@slatebridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — Q4 peak and SLO target

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re evaluating a Dedicated capacity commitment for SlateBridge (customer search + summarization flows). A few specifics from our side:

- Expected peak window: weeknights 20:00–23:00 PT during Q4 (holiday spike).
- Estimated active users at peak: 85k MAU with a bursting bot population — we estimate 1.2M generation requests/day during peak week.
- Typical request size: prompt ~120 tokens, average completion ~180 tokens (total ~300 tokens per request).
- SLO target: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 350 ms for interactive tier.

Can you provide a rough committed-slab sizing and an initial tokens/sec / headroom estimate we can use for procurement? Attaching our rough telemetry snapshot.

Cheers,
Elena

[Attachment: slatebridge_peak_profile.csv (csv)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@slatebridge.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@slatebridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Q4 peak and SLO target

Elena — thanks, this helps. Quick first-pass sizing and assumptions below (sharing transparently so procurement can budget while we finalize the mutual action plan):

Assumptions (first-pass):
- Model baseline: 7B encoder-decoder style for search+summaries (throughput-oriented profile).
- Avg tokens/request: 300 tokens (per your note).
- Mean tokens/sec per GPU: ~1100 tokens/sec for the chosen 7B baseline on our optimized runtime (single-stream inference, p95-optimized kernels).
- Effective tokens/sec per slab (8x A5000-equivalent GPUs): ~8,800 tokens/sec (1100 * 8).

Peak math (targeting p95 <= 350 ms):
- Peak QPS (requests/sec) = peak req/day window / seconds in peak window. With 1.2M requests/day concentrated into a 3-hr nightly window, approximate 1.2M / (3*3600) ≈ 111 requests/sec sustained during the window, peak bursts up to ~450 req/sec.
- Token load at sustained = 111 req/sec * 300 tokens = 33,300 tokens/sec.
- Token load at burst = 450 req/sec * 300 tokens = 135,000 tokens/sec.

Slab sizing: (sustained) 33,300 / 8,800 ≈ 3.8 slabs → round up to 4 slabs.
(surge headroom) 135,000 / 8,800 ≈ 15.3 slabs → to meet peak bursts without queuing we'd need ~16 slabs, which is probably cost-prohibitive as a firm commit.

Recommended committed configuration (balanced):
- Committed: 6 slabs (48 GPUs) — covers sustained + steady growth with ~66% headroom against sustained and allows warm KV/prefix cache to absorb a chunk of burst traffic.
- Burst policy: autoscale burst pool up to 14 slabs (112 GPUs) during defined peak windows (billing for burst on metered rate), with an agreement on maximum burst frequency.
- Engineering mitigations: KV prefix caching for repeated search prompts, batching for async summarization workloads, and a short request-priority queue for interactive flows.
- Latency expectation: with 6 committed slabs + warm caches, we expect p95 to be within target for sustained traffic; under full-burst (no autoscale) p95 will increase unless burst capacity is provisioned.

Deliverables: I’ll put this into a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and include a conservative SLA/commit recommendation. If useful, we can model two scenarios (lean commit + frequent burst vs. large commit + smaller metered burst).

Attaching a one-page MAP skeleton and the rough workbook. Can you confirm whether SlateBridge prefers capped-dollar bursts or pay-as-you-go metered bursts?

Best,
Ben

[Attachment: SlateBridge_MutualActionPlan_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateBridge dedicated sizing — throughput, SLO fit, buffer proposal

Ben — couple of notes from infra sizing side:

- GPU throughput: 1100 tps baseline is conservative for 7B; if we enable 4-bit quantization (Q4) and the customer's payloads have low dynamic range, we can push effective tokens/sec per GPU to ~1,700 (x1.55) in steady-state, which shifts slab math significantly. Recommend including a quantized run option in the MAP as an opt-in.
- Cache impact: their telemetry shows 28% repeat prompts in the last 7 days. With KV/prefix caching warm we can shave ~25–35% off token compute for those hits. That materially reduces burst slab needs.
- Warmup time: for autoscale, ensure we reserve a small warmup lane (2 GPUs) for low-latency interactive requests during scale-up; cold-starting entire slabs will cause transient p95 spikes.
- Operational buffer: instead of 66% headroom, suggest committing to 50% headroom and defining explicit burst SLA terms (e.g., up to 12 burst slabs per night, >12 requires pre-notification). This is a commercial tradeoff that procurement will like.

If Ben agrees, we'll update the spreadsheet with Q4 scenario math showing both quantized and fp16 footprints, and a recommended contract clause for burst gating.

—Kimberly & Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@slatebridge.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@slatebridge.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateBridge dedicated sizing — throughput, SLO fit, buffer proposal

Elena — quick recap and proposed next steps after internal sizing review:

What we recommend (finalized proposal):
1) Committed: 6 slabs (48 GPUs) — covers sustained nightly load with ~50% operational headroom assuming warm KV cache and modest batching for async workloads.
2) Burst: Autoscale pool up to 12 additional slabs (96 GPUs) for certified peak windows (nightly 20:00–23:00 PT during Q4). Bursts beyond this require pre-approval and will be metered at the burst rate.
3) Performance optimizations: Offer a Q4 trial enabling Q4 quantization on 50% of traffic (opt-in) — expected effective improvement ~1.5x tokens/sec/GPU for eligible requests.
4) SLO: Target p95 <= 350 ms for interactive tier under committed + burst policy with the warmup lane kept active. We’ll monitor and create regression alerts tied to the MAP test prompts.

Commercial note: The recommended commit + capped burst model is intended to balance predictable cost and achievable latency targets. If SlateBridge prefers predictable flat capacity for the entire burst window, we can price a 14-slab committed option.

Next steps:
- I’ve uploaded the MAP draft and the scenario workbook to the HubSpot deal (link below). Please confirm whether you want capped-dollar bursts or metered bursts; procurement will need that to finalize contract terms.
- If you confirm, I’ll route the draft MAP for signatures and schedule a 30-min tech walkthrough with our infra team (Kimberly/Karthik) the week of Oct 4.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/DBL-9032 (MAP + workbook)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/SlateBridge-MAP-v1

Thanks — happy to chat through the slab math live if helpful.

Best,
Ben
